comment: Documents for the edit sweep (sweep.test.ts) beside the shared CriticMarkup corpus: lists with star, plus and odd-numbered markers, tables with alignment colons, backslashed pipes and uneven padding, nested and quoted lists, syntax the serializer writes differently from the source, a mark across list items, a CRLF document, literal openers of every mark kind, a literal replacement opener with a later closer, blocks sharing a line run, reference links, task lists with strikethrough and a footnote, and a sample review.

cases.name: review sample
cases.in:
# Design note: artifact review {++(draft)++}

This note shows {==every kind of mark==}{>>Is this list complete? Check against critic.ts.<<} that the review editor has to render.
The hub stores Markdown with {~~CriticMark~>CriticMarkup~~} inline, and a reviewer can {--simply --}suggest edits.

## Marks

- An insertion: we {++really ++}need this.
- A deletion: this is {--not --}optional.
- A substitution: the {~~quick~>slow~~} path.
- A lone comment after a word{>>Who owns this?<<}.
* A highlight on its own: {==important==}.

1. Ordered item with `inline code` and a {++suggested `flag`++}.
2. Marks inside code are literal: `{++not a mark++}`.
3. A mark may hold a code span: {--the `old` flag--}.

## Table

| Mark | Syntax | Render |
|:-----|:------:|-------:|
| insertion | `{++text++}` | {++green++} |
| deletion | `{--text--}` | {--red--} |
| comment | `{>>note<<}` | margin note{>>like this<<} |

## Code

```go
// Tokens in fenced code stay literal: {--keep me--}
func main() { fmt.Println("{~~a~>b~~}") }
```

A mark may span lines: {++this insertion
continues on the next line++} and ends here.

> A quote with _emphasis_, **strong** and a {--stale--} word.

An unclosed token at the end is literal text: {++ dangling.
